result:
The REST module calls `OrderService.getOrderTypes` in three production places and in one test controller. I traced the direct callers only. The `OrderService.getOrderTypes(boolean includeRetired)` declaration is at `openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/OrderService.java:811`, and `OrderServiceImpl`, `OrderDAO` and `HibernateOrderDAO` implement or declare the same signature. I did not check whether `openmrs-esm-patient-chart` calls the REST endpoints, and I did not search other repositories beyond these two.

**Confirmed affected (production code)**

1. **`openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_10/OrderTypeResource1_10.java`**, lines 120-123 (`doGetAll`). Lists all order types for the `/ordertype` resource, passing `context.getIncludeAll()` as `includeRetired`. A change to the retired-filtering behaviour changes the list returned by `GET /ordertype`.
2. **Same file**, lines 128-139 (`doSearch`). Calls `getOrderTypes(context.getIncludeAll())` and then filters the result by the `q` parameter in memory. A change to the returned set changes the `?q=` search results too.
3. **`openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_10/OrderableResource1_10.java`**, lines 64-70 (`search`). Calls `getOrderTypes(false)`, so it only ever sees active order types, and passes the result to `getOrderableConceptClasses(orderTypes)`. A change to the active-only set, or to what counts as "active", changes which concept classes this search returns.

**Confirmed affected (tests)**

4. **`openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs1_10/OrderTypeController1_10Test.java`**, lines 53-56 (`getAllCount`), 95-100 (`shouldListAllOrderTypesIncludingRetiredOnesIfIncludeAllIsSetToTrue`), and 144-158 (`shouldCreateANewOrderType`). These compare REST results against `getOrderTypes(false)` and `getOrderTypes(true)` counts. Any behaviour change will show up as failures here first.

**Excluded (name clash)**

- `openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/parameter/OrderSearchCriteria.java:198` declares a different `getOrderTypes()` with no arguments. It is not `OrderService.getOrderTypes` and is not called from the REST module.

**Not checked**

- Whether any other REST module code reaches `getOrderTypes` through a non-literal path, such as reflection, a generic resource base class, or a Spring-wired proxy. The text search found nothing of that kind, but I did not verify it.
- The `openmrs-module-reportingrest` repository, which exists in Falkon and may consume the REST module's order-type resources. I did not search it.
- Callers of the REST `/ordertype` and `/orderable` endpoints outside the Java code, such as the frontend. The question covers the REST module only.
